newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine 12-month T-bill yields seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine 12-month T-bill yields seen falling.

text.p: Yields on six- and nine-month Ukrainian Treasury bills should remain stable this week while 12-month yields are expected to drop on central bank buying, analysts and dealers said on Tuesday.
"It should be an interesting week," said Patricia Bartholemew, senior analyst at Wood and Company. "Twelve-month is where the action will be this week."
Bartholomew said the National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) held 135 million hryvnias ($72.8 million), or 76 percent, of the 177 million hryvnias of T-bills maturing this week.

"This will not have much of an impact on six- and nine-month yields," she said. "But there could be a rollover of NBU bills to 12-month, which means the volume will go up and rates will be at 28-29 percent."

The average yield on 12-month yields eased to 30.46 percent from 30.75 percent at the last auction, while six-month paper firmed to 20.13 percent from 20.00 percent and nine-month paper was unchanged at 28.13 percent. Yields have more than halved since the start of the year.
Jurgen Conrad, Deutsche Bank Research economist and member of the German Advisory Group on Economic Reforms, also said a very active central bank could strongly move T-bill yields.
"In a word, everything is possible," he said.

But he said six-month yields were unlikely to drop further because they were already low, on par with the most recent annual inflation forecast of 15 to 16 percent made by Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko last month.
He said the influence of the central bank, which is allowed to buy one-third of all Treasury bills sold this year to finance the budget deficit, would not lower yields much further.

"They have been buying to create stability and bring yields down a little more," he said. "But they don't want to throw all Ukrainians and foreign participants out of the market and in order to do (that, the central bank) won't bring interest rates down any further."
Alexander Okhrymenko, dealer at Banque Societe Generale Ukraine, also expected T-bills yields to remain about steady.

"Today there are few non-residents buying, but on Thursday, there will be more. Today, it's possible yields will rise, but on Thursday, they could fall. This is a purely technical situation tied in with volume of demand," he said.
Analysts said central bank activity on the T-bill market would also mean a stable or slightly firmer hryvnia.
Okhrymenko expected the hryvnia to only stray a bit from its current level this month and next.
The hryvnia was unchanged on Tuesday at 1.8570 on the Ukrainian Interbank Currency Exchange.
"This week does not differ from last week," Okhtymenko said. "There are lots of dollars and not enough hryvnias."
